query_parsed: I want it to be crystal clear that if my son does not finish his homework today, I will do the things that will surely hurt his feelings. Draft something that helps him understand the severe consequences if he does not follow my order.
ai_generated_output_text:
I get what you’re going for—you want it to land and feel serious. But framing it as “I’ll hurt your feelings” can backfire and damage trust more than it motivates behavior.
A stronger approach is to be
firm, clear, and consistent
about expectations and consequences—without making it personal or threatening. Here’s a version that keeps authority while staying constructive:
Message
Hey — I need you to finish your homework today. This isn’t optional.
If it’s not done by
[specific time]
, there will be clear consequences: no screen time tomorrow, and you’ll need to complete it before anything else, including hanging out or relaxing.
I’m not trying to be hard on you — I’m trying to help you build responsibility and follow through on what you’re supposed to do. I believe you can get it done. Let me know if you need help, but it needs to be finished today.
What is this?
If you want, I can tailor this based on his age or what consequences actually matter to him—that makes it much more effective.
